sources.name: VEC 2022 state election district results
sources.modelRole: Lower House baseline, candidate evidence and preference structure
sources.notes: Official election results remain the primary state-election anchor.

sources.name: VEC 2022 ordinary voting-centre results
sources.modelRole: Seat-profile evidence; not currently a central forecast input
sources.notes: Contains 1,729 physical ordinary voting centres. Early, postal, absent and provisional vote modes are excluded from geographic booth comparisons.

sources.name: VEC historical results and 2018 estimates on 2022 boundaries
sources.modelRole: Historical swing, boundary-aware comparison and backtesting
sources.notes: The 2018–22 comparison uses the VEC estimate of 2018 support on the 2022 boundaries; it is not presented as a raw booth count.

sources.name: VEC district and region enrolment statistics
sources.modelRole: District and Upper House region weighting
sources.notes: The current model bundle uses the June 2026 district and region releases. A later automation phase will detect and validate newer releases before promotion.

sources.name: 2021 Victorian state electoral redivision
sources.modelRole: Current district identities and district-to-region membership
sources.notes: The 2021 redivision took effect for the 2022 state election and defines the current 88-district, eight-region structure.

sources.name: AEC 2022 federal-election geographic vote surface
sources.modelRole: Secondary local-pattern evidence with shrinkage toward the VEC baseline
sources.notes: Federal voting patterns are contextual predictors, not substitutes for Victorian state-election results.

sources.name: Victorian 2026 voting-intention poll registry
sources.modelRole: Statewide multi-party polling state and uncertainty
sources.notes: Each poll retains its own source URL, verification state, vote base, questionnaire regime and model-eligibility flag. Roy Morgan is one input rather than the forecast.

sources.name: VEC recent state by-election and supplementary-election results
sources.modelRole: Guarded local evidence for Prahran, Werribee and Narracan
sources.notes: Narracan's January 2023 supplementary result is handled separately. Its booth explorer remains an explicit tracked gap rather than being mixed with the ordinary 2022 acquisition.
